Category A: All staff positions, regardless of remote work eligibility, require an initial 30-calendar-day on-campus work period. Based on an evaluation by the supervisor and area Vice President, this position is classified as Category A as de fined in the College’s Remote Work Policy , without occasional ad-hoc remote work flexibility. Your position is essential to on-campus operations and requires you to work exclusively on campus Your standard working hours, days, and hours may vary due to the needs of the department or the College. All remote work arrangements, including ad-hoc remote work, must be approved by the direct supervisor, area Cabinet member, and Human Resources, and are subject to periodic review based on institutional needs. These arrangements are neither guaranteed nor considered entitlements and may change due to factors such as employee performance, evolving business needs, or changes to the position.

Education : Any combination of education and training that provides the required knowledge, skills, and ability for the position.
Positions are benefits eligible and include day, swing, and evening shifts, and may vary or change at any time due to the needs of the College and department.
Experience : None.
In the dish room, receive soiled dishes, trays, flatware, glassware, pots, pans, utensils, other kitchen equipment.
and prepare them for washing by scraping off food and other debris. Sort, wash and sanitize soiled items using appropriate methods and procedures for each item.
Assure proper temperature of dishwashing machinery and water as defined by Health Department regulations. Log final rinse temperatures as directed by manager(s).
Sort items when cleaned and restock service areas and kitchen before, during and after each service period. Sort and return catering china, flatware, and glassware to the catering stockroom.
Follow proper wash, rinse, and sanitize process when using a three - compartment sink and fill out Sanitizer Solution Dispenser Log.
Properly store, label, dispense, use, and dispose of cleaning chemicals.

Sweep and mop floors as directed by managers, including walk-in refrigerators, dining room, servery, and kitchen. Maintain cleanliness of work areas, including walls, trash cans, dishwashing machinery, dish belt, and work tables.

Remove trash generated by staff and customers from kitchen and serving areas to proper disposal containers. Maintain cleanliness of the dock, trash bins, and surrounding areas. Break down cardboard and stow in proper disposal or recycling container(s). Clean ovens, drains, floor mats, grills, exhaust filters, and other kitchen equipment as directed.
Participate in required department training related to food safety, chemical safety, equipment operation, workplace safety, emergency procedures and department standards.
Follow the established cleaning and station assignment calendar to ensure all assigned areas and tasks are completed according to schedule.
Perform additional cleaning, sanitation, setup, breakdown, stocking, and operational support duties as assigned by management.
As specifically assigned by a manager or supervisor, assist with floor attendant duties during service periods, and assist with special event or catering setups.
As specifically assigned by a manager, assist in loading and unloading trucks, setup of tables, set up of banquets, and preparation of beverages.
As specifically assigned by a manager, maintain cleanliness of restrooms.
Performs other duties as assigned.
Employees in this position usually work with a team but may occasionally work alone. Most work is done indoors, but some activities occur outdoors. Not all facilities are air-conditioned.
The essential function of this job requires work to be performed on campus.

Must be able to stand, walk, bend, climb, push, pull, stoop, twist, stretch, squat, reach and lift to 50 pounds from floor to waist level without assistance, climb ladders up to 25 feet with assistance and up to 10 feet unassisted, and be able to work on feet for prolonged periods of time.
Must be able to understand and follow basic instructions in oral and written English.
Must be able to read analog thermometers and maintain written records of temperatures.
Must be able to establish and maintain cooperative working relationships.
Must be able to work well without continuous supervision.
Must wear required uniforms, personal protective equipment (PPE), and other safety gear as required.
Requires physical fitness and ability to learn safe food handling and production methods as defined by the College/Dining Services management.
Good personal hygiene is required.

Maintain the ability, and will be expected to work overtime in emergency situations and during special events as specified by management, for example (commencement, family weekend, alumni week, admitted student week, Board of Trustees weeks, etc.)
